claim: A third of excess deaths in the United States between 1 March and  1 August 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic could not be directly attributed to the coronavirus
justification: A JAMA study published on October 12, 2020, analyzed 225,530 excess deaths in the U.S. between March 1 and August 1, 2020, using data from the [National Center for Health Statistics and the U.S. Census Bureau](https://www.cnn.com/2020/10/12/health/us-deaths-covid-19-pandemic-jama-study/index.html). It found that 150,541 (67%) were directly attributed to COVID-19, leaving approximately 33% (one-third) not directly attributed to the coronavirus. This remainder includes deaths indirectly caused by the pandemic, such as from delayed medical care or drug overdoses, as noted in [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/covid-19-pandemic-has-claimed-far-more-lives-reported-study-n1242970). The claim aligns precisely with this study, and no evidence contradicts it.

claim: Prominent US Democrat party members including Hillary and Bill Clinton, were running a child sex-trafficking ring in the basement of a Washington, D.C., pizzeria.
justification: The claim is a baseless conspiracy theory known as "Pizzagate," which has been thoroughly debunked. The allegedly implicated pizzeria, Comet Ping Pong, "doesn’t even have a basement" ([The Cut](https://www.thecut.com/2016/12/to-understand-pizzagate-it-helps-to-understand-cults.html)), and no law enforcement investigations found any evidence of sex-trafficking ([NPR](https://www.npr.org/2016/11/27/503489400/fake-news-surge-pins-d-c-pizzeria-as-home-to-child-trafficking)). Neither Hillary nor Bill Clinton have ever been charged or formally accused of any crime related to child sex-trafficking ([USA Today](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/06/21/fact-check-hillary-clinton-wasnt-court-testifying-june-2/3199725001/)), and the story originated from false online rumors on platforms like 4chan ([PolitiFact](https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2020/oct/07/facebook-posts/four-years-later-theres-still-no-evidence-support-/)). All evidence explicitly refutes the allegation, leading to a final verdict of `refuted`.
gt_justification: The sources show that this claim is incorrect and is false news so the claim is refuted.

claim: Anthony Weiner’s laptop contained proof Hillary Clinton & her associates are involved in child trafficking & paedophilia

While Anthony Weiner's laptop was seized by the FBI, the investigation targeted Weiner's own sexual misconduct, not Hillary Clinton or her associates. No official charges, indictments, or public statements have ever linked the laptop's contents to child trafficking or pedophilia involving Clinton. The sources for the allegation consist solely of anonymous, unverified reports from the disreputable website True Pundit and an online forum. Credible news organizations did not report the claim, and PolitiFact rated it "Pants on Fire," explicitly calling it a rumor or hoax [PolitiFact](https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2016/nov/04/conservative-daily-post/evidence-ridiculously-thin-sensational-claim-huge-/). The FBI itself declined to confirm any such investigation. Therefore, the claim is false.

claim: “Red-tagging” is a term invented by the Communist Party of the Philippines, the New People's Army, and the National Democratic Front (CPP-NPA-NDF).
justification: The term "red-tagging" is a well-documented, long-standing practice used by state actors against alleged communists, with historical roots in the 1950s Philippines and parallels to McCarthyism, not a term invented by the CPP-NPA-NDF. Multiple sources, such as [Wikipedia](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/Red-tagging_in_the_Philippines) and the [BBC](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-54144623), describe it as a government-led tactic used against left-leaning individuals and groups, and no evidence was found that the CPP-NPA-NDF coined the term. The claim's author, Lorraine Badoy, provided no supporting evidence for her assertion during a Senate budget hearing.

“Red-tagging” has been in existence before  CPP-NPA-NDF were founded.

The report that her family spent Christmas with the Obamas in 2012 is supported by a news article ([source](https://nypost.com/2020/10/17/kristen-welker-next-debate-moderator-has-deep-democrat-ties/)), but this does not offset the false statements about donations and current party affiliation. Therefore, the overall claim is refuted.

claim: In the US lockdowns are partly responsible for excess deaths not directly attributed to COVID-19 which were observed in 2020.
justification: The fact-check found that in the US, excess deaths not directly attributed to COVID-19 in 2020 were substantial—33% of ~225,530 excess deaths per a [JAMA study](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2771761) and ~100,947 per the [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/69/wr/pdfs/mm6942e2-H.pdf). A [medRxiv study](https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.06.26.20098434v1.full) directly documents a mechanism linking lockdowns to these deaths: a 43.8% reduction in acute medical admissions and more than double the risk of in-hospital death from delayed care for time-sensitive conditions like heart attacks. Other sources note that non-COVID excess deaths could reflect pandemic disruptions, including stay-at-home orders, but do not isolate lockdown effects from other pandemic factors. While no rigorous causal analysis separates lockdowns from broader pandemic impacts, the documented pathway via delayed medical care supports the claim that lockdowns were partly responsible. Thus, the claim is **supported**.
gt_justification: The Q&A's only mention excess death due to covid and so no data for other causes such as the claimed 'lockdowns' so more evidence is needed.

claim: Pennsylvania US rejects 372,000 mail-in ballots.
justification: The fact-check reveals that Pennsylvania rejected 372,000 **requests** for mail-in ballots, not the ballots themselves; over 90% of these were duplicate applications ([ProPublica](https://www.propublica.org/article/pennsylvanias-rejection-of-372-000-ballot-applications-bewilders-voters-and-strains-election-staff), [The Philadelphia Inquirer](https://www.inquirer.com/politics/election/pennsylvania-mail-ballot-rejections-duplicate-applications-20201016.html)). The claim falsely labels these as rejected ballots, misrepresenting the data. The verdict is therefore refuted.

claim: It's unclear how Joe Biden acquired his recent wealth since leaving office in 2017
justification: Publicly available tax returns and financial disclosures, along with credible media reports from the [Associated Press](https://www.bostonglobe.com/news/politics/2019/07/09/biden-earned-millions-after-leaving-white-house-financial-disclosures-show/YDpLcGshpG7pJNzrTTRgWO/story.html), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/michelatindera/2019/07/10/bidens-made-nearly-twice-as-much-in-2017-than-previous-19-years-combined/), and [VOA](https://www.voanews.com/a/usa_us-politics_biden-and-wife-made-more-15m-after-leaving-office/6171514.html), document that Joe Biden’s post‑2017 wealth came from transparent sources: approximately $13.2 million from book deals, over $2.4 million from speaking engagements, and about $775,000 from a professorship at the University of Pennsylvania, with Jill Biden contributing at least $700,000 from her own speaking fees. No undisclosed or mysterious income sources were found, and no official investigations were necessary because the earnings are fully accounted for in his [publicly filed tax returns and financial disclosure forms](http://www.disclosures.org/joe-biden-financial-disclosures/). Thus, the claim that his wealth accumulation is “unclear” is refuted.
gt_justification: He made $15.6 million in the 2 years after he left office mostly through speaking fees

claim: India's Congress party candidate Maskoor Usmani installed Jinnah's portrait at AMU.
justification: The portrait of Muhammad Ali Jinnah has been a historical fixture at Aligarh Muslim University’s students’ union hall since 1938, when Jinnah was granted life membership—long before any involvement by Maskoor Usmani. The university administration (spokesperson Shafey Kidwai and Vice Chancellor Tariq Mansoor) explicitly stated that Usmani did not install it, and Usmani himself denied the allegation, calling it a “blatant lie.” No photographic, video, or eyewitness evidence supports the claim, and the only outlet that reported it (AajTak) was found false by fact-checkers. The claim is therefore contradicted by all available evidence. [Source](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/aajtaks-claim-that-maskoor-usmani-hung-jinnah-portrait-at-amu-is-false)
gt_justification: The portrait of Jinnah has been on display at AMU since 1938, so India's Congress party candidate Maskoor Usmani could not have installed it. Hence, the claim is refuted.

claim: Most deaths in the 1918 influenza pandemic originated from bacterial pneumonia caused by face masks and that Dr Anthony Fauci, the US government’s top expert in the fight against Covid-19, knew about it.
justification: The claim is refuted. Peer-reviewed research consistently shows that the vast majority of deaths in the 1918 influenza pandemic resulted from secondary bacterial pneumonia following influenza virus infection, not from face masks [New Scientist](https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn14458-bacteria-were-the-real-killers-in-1918-flu-pandemic/) [NIH](https://www.nih.gov/news-events/news-releases/bacterial-pneumonia-caused-most-deaths-1918-influenza-pandemic). A 2008 study co-authored by Dr. Anthony Fauci confirmed that more than 90% of deaths were due to bacterial pneumonia after the virus damaged the respiratory tract [CIDRAP](https://www.cidrap.umn.edu/influenza-vaccines/study-bacterial-pneumonia-was-main-killer-1918-flu-pandemic). No evidence links mask-wearing to increased bacterial pneumonia; the complication occurred regardless of mask use [NIH](https://www.nih.gov/news-events/news-releases/bacterial-pneumonia-caused-most-deaths-1918-influenza-pandemic). Furthermore, Fauci’s research and public health guidance do not implicate face masks as a cause of death [JSTOR](https://daily.jstor.org/anthony-s-fauci-on-pandemic-preparedness/). The claim therefore has no factual basis.
gt_justification: there is no evidence this happened in 1918, and no evidence that mask wearing causes bacterial pneumonia.

claim: BJP MP Kirron Kher Said "Rape Is A Part Of Indian Culture And It Can't Be Stopped"
justification: The claim is false: Kirron Kher never said "Rape Is A Part Of Indian Culture And It Can't Be Stopped." The attributed quote is a distortion, and no verified video or audio of the alleged statement exists.
gt_justification: The MP has said comments about rape but not the phrase that it can not be stopped. The claim was also on a Facebook page that spreads fake news.

claim: A message will be sent to your phone claiming to show that the Covid19 curve is flattening in India, But It will contain a malicious file

gt_justification: QA pairs state it is fake.
